🚨🚨BREAKING UPDATES 🚨 

🇵🇭 Death Toll Climbs to 11 in Philippines Landfill Disaster
Cebu City, Philippines 

A tragic collapse at a large landfill in Cebu City has now claimed 11 lives, with more than 20 people still missing. The incident happened at the Binaliw landfill, where heavy rain in recent weeks made the piles of trash unstable and heavier, leading to the slide.

Rescue teams have been working hard but hopes of finding more survivors are fading after three days. They have already saved 12 injured people from the rubble. A local fire official said it's unlikely anyone else is still alive under the debris.

The government has stepped in quickly. The company running the landfill, Prime Integrated Waste Solutions, has been told to stop operations and fix any issues within 90 days. Officials will investigate what went wrong and hold those responsible accountable.

Lawmakers are calling for big changes to how the country handles waste, including better safety for workers at these sites. This isn't the first time something like this has happened in the Philippines, where big cities like Cebu rely on huge landfills for trash.

People on social media are sharing sadness and anger, with some blaming poor management. Experts say better rules and checks could prevent future tragedies. Updates are expected as the search continues.

Source: BBC World

LOOK: Temporary road closures and heavy traffic are expected on January 15, 2026, starting at 3:00 a.m., for the annual Walk with Mary, the Cebu City Transportation Office said. 

The procession will pass through Guadalupe Church, B. Rodriguez Street, Osmeña Boulevard, and end at the Basilica Minore del Santo Niño. 

Traffic personnel will be deployed, and motorists are advised to take alternate routes and allow extra travel time on the said date. | 📷: CCTO #CDNDigital
